newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil trade gaps seen continuing for some time.
newsitem.headline: Brazil trade gaps seen continuing for some time.

text.p: The Brazilian government expects to continue to post monthly trade deficits for a considerable period of time until structural problems in the economy are rectified, said a senior trade official.
Helio Mauro Franca, director of the ministry's department of foreign trade policy, said monthly trade gaps, even if they reach $1.0 billion or more, were not considered a problem.
"We still have a situation in which deficits will occur for a long period of time. You can't solve import-export problems overnight," Franca told Reuters.
Franca was quoted by the Jornal do Brasil newspaper over the weekend as saying he expected monthly deficits for the next two years to be between $800 million and $1.0 billion.
But he said he had been slightly misinterpreted and had merely insisted that deficits of that order were not a concern.
"The deficits are not a problem, they are normal," Franca said, pointing out that the government had taken measures to boost exports but these would take time to have an effect.
The trade balance for 1996, seen at up to $5.2 billion, is expected to be released around mid-month.
